notes.decision: Standard Coptic citation formula 'this name (namely)': ⲡⲓ-ⲣⲉⲛ ('this name') + ⲭⲉ (= ϫⲉ, citation particle). The chapter heading inquires into the meaning of the divine titles 'rich god' and 'angel.'

Rendered 'this (one) to whom name is given.' ϯⲣⲉⲛ ('give name,' in glossary as ϯⲡⲉⲛ) idiomatic for 'name, call'; ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to him.' The Illuminator opens the inquiry into divine titles uttered by men in the cosmos.
Translated 'uttering it with their mouths.' ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ 'utter, send forth' (in glossary) + ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ 'it' + ⲍⲛ-ⲣⲱⲟⲩ 'in/with their mouths.'

The line begins mid-sentence, continuing from the previous page. ⲁⲣⲁⲩ ('to/regarding them') with ⲭⲉ introducing direct quotation: '...regarding them, saying: They are gods of gods.' The construction 'gods of gods' (genitive plural) parallels later 'rich of rich' and 'angels' in the descending hierarchy.

Idiom ⲥⲉϩⲉ + ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ = 'set on the feet of, cause to stand upright' (cf. accumulated ⲥⲉⲍⲱ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗). Translated 'set upright' to preserve the vertical-cosmological semantics; the Father raises these beings into existence before the cosmic Likeness.
Reading uncertain. Tentatively analyzed as ⲉ-ⲡⲉ-ⲗⲁⲏ ('to the people,' Greek λαός; cf. accumulated ⲗⲁⲏ → 'people'). Could alternatively be a corrupt or unique form. Translated 'to the people' for now.

Reading uncertain. Paired with ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧϥ̄ ('stillness'), context demands a complementary ecclesial-cosmic quality. Possibly from ⲧⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ ('persuasion, agreement') or related to ϩⲏⲧ ('heart, foremost'). Translated 'concord' tentatively.

Lycopolitan reflex of Greek ἀλλάσσω 'exchange, alter' (reduplicated/intensive form). In Manichaean context this denotes souls subject to metempsychosis/transmutation, captured and exchanged through bodily transmigration in the realm of the Enemy. Cf. accumulated ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('exchange/transmutation').

Reading 'of the Spirit' (= ⲙ̄ⲡⲡ̄ⲛ̄ⲁ̄, with ⲡⲧⲛⲁ as a Lyc. orthographic rendering of ⲡⲡⲛⲁ 'the Spirit'). Cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲡⲛⲁⲃ̄ ⲙⲡ̄ⲛⲁ 'the Great One of the Spirit.' Alternative reading would be 'of the Mercy' (ⲛⲁ root) or scribal anticipation of another title (the leer suggests scribal abandonment). The combined reading 'house of the Greatness, of the Spirit' fits the standard Manichaean Father-of-Greatness epithet.

ⲉⲧⲟⲓ̈ ⲛⲉⲁⲩ = 'who is of glory' (ⲛⲉⲁⲩ = ⲛ̄ⲉⲟⲟⲩ); standard descriptor of the Third Ambassador as the glorious cosmic envoy. Completes the trinity of cosmic houses: Greatness/Spirit (gods) — Beloved of Lights (angels) — Ambassador of Glory (rich-ones).
